Getting Started with dbVisuals

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Introduction

dbVisuals is a Canvas visualization workspace built on SQLRooms for interactive exploration of dbverse data. This submission branch excludes AI and arbitrary R-code execution.

dbVisuals features

  • Dropzone - Drag and drop files directly into the UI for exploration
  • SQL Editor - Run queries on database-backed objects
  • Hardware-accelerated Visualizations - High-performance WebGL spatial rendering using deck.gl
  • Interactive Linked Views - Create interactive linked visualizations using Mosaic specs
  • Live Connection - Call the UI from R
  • Smart Chart Builder - Easily create charts based on common data in your database

Installation 

# Install the reviewed local checkout; this repository is still private.
remotes::install_local("r-package")

# Optional: Install all recommended dependencies
library(dbVisuals)
install_dbvisuals_deps()

dbVisuals automatically provides access to:

  • rDeckgl - R interface to deck.gl for WebGL visualizations
  • rMosaic - R interface to Mosaic for interactive linked views

Quick Start

Launch with In-Memory Database

Without a native database file, the workspace uses browser-local DuckDB-WASM and the bundled demonstration tables. Imported files stay in the browser and are not synchronized back into the R session.

library(dbVisuals)

# Launch the standalone browser workspace
dashboard <- launchBrowser()

Launch with GiottoDB Database

For spatial data analysis, connect to a GiottoDB database from (Giotto Suite)[https://giottosuite.com]

library(dbVisuals)
library(GiottoDB)
library(GiottoData)
library(duckdb)

# Create a GiottoDB database
gobject <- loadGiottoMini("visium")
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), dbdir = "my_spatial_data.duckdb")
gobject_db <- as_giottodb(gobject, con = con, temporary = FALSE)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

# Launch dbVisuals
dashboard <- launchBrowser(db_path = "my_spatial_data.duckdb")

# Explore your spatial data with SQL queries and visualizations

Cleanup

When you’re done, clean up the background processes:

stop_sqlrooms(dashboard)

What You Can Do in dbVisuals

1. SQL Queries on Spatial Data

Run SQL queries directly on your GiottoDB tables:

-- Query your GiottoDB tables
SELECT * FROM gdb_cell_rna_raw LIMIT 10;

-- Aggregate spatial expression data
SELECT cell_ID, COUNT(*) as gene_count
FROM gdb_cell_rna_normalized
GROUP BY cell_ID;

-- Spatial polygon queries
SELECT poly_ID, ST_Area(geom) as area
FROM gdb_poly_cell;

2. Interactive Visualizations

Create deck.gl and Mosaic visualizations using the built-in tools in dbVisuals. Use Add Chart for Spatial Map and Table as well as ordinary Mosaic charts. For native R-backed data, prepare the database and close its writer connection before launching. Stop the workspace before modifying the file from R, then close the connection and relaunch. Concurrent cross-process writes are not promised.

Advanced Configuration

Custom Ports

Specify custom ports if defaults are in use:

dashboard <- launchBrowser(
  db_path = "my_data.duckdb",
  port = 3002,           # R server port
  frontend_port = 5174,  # Frontend port
  browser = TRUE         # Auto-open browser
)

One instance at a time

The running server and front end are tracked in a single package-level slot, so launching a second workspace stops the first one even when the ports differ: after the second launchBrowser() below, port 5173 is no longer served and stop_sqlrooms(dashboard1) reports “No running SQL Rooms processes found”.

dashboard1 <- launchBrowser(db_path = "project1.duckdb",
                            port = 3001, frontend_port = 5173)

# This replaces dashboard1 rather than running alongside it.
dashboard2 <- launchBrowser(db_path = "project2.duckdb",
                            port = 3002, frontend_port = 5174)

To work with two databases at once, run them from two separate R sessions.

Troubleshooting

Ports Already in Use

If you see connection errors, try different ports:

launchBrowser(port = 3002, frontend_port = 5174)

Missing Dependencies

Install recommended packages for full functionality:

install_dbvisuals_deps()

Or manually:

install.packages(c("DBI", "duckdb", "shiny", "rDeckgl", "rMosaic"))
